status: G4 rest: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g4-ox-dark, in Chapters VIII and X (the desktop app only)
use: A dark draught ox, unyoked, paired with the grey ox beside the ox cart in the quartermaster's court beyond the board (Chapters VIII and X).

generator.prompt: A Roman draught ox of the mid-3rd century AD standing square: all four legs straight and vertical, evenly spaced, head held level and facing forward, tail hanging straight down, symmetrical. A heavy, deep-chested working ox about 1.45 metres at the withers with a dark chestnut-brown coat shading to near black on the neck and shoulders, a paler muzzle, a loose dewlap, medium-length upward-curving pale horns with dark tips and a plain hemp rope halter. No yoke, no harness, no cart, no plough, no rider, no people. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate. Single isolated model with complete geometry from every side and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above. No ground plane, no display plinth, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the camps in the desktop build at High
review.notes: As asked: dark chestnut shading to near black at the neck and shoulders, a pale muzzle, pale horns with dark tips and a rope halter. It came standing askew in its file, 59 degrees round from facing +x, and was turned to face +x: 2.24 m long and 1.6 m to its horn tips. Kept with a note: under its belly, between the hind legs, is a small pale udder, which the negative prompt named. Beside Chapter VIII's ox cart it stands with the pilot's pale grey ox, the pair now plainly two beasts; the udder does not show from the camp camera.
